rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, there is no evidence to guide exploitation, so the priority is establishing a clean, interpretable baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest RNA configuration: PCA is a standard, fast linear encoder unlikely to be a bottleneck, and singleprofile avoids confounding from aggregation. This gives a well-defined reference accuracy for RNA alone, against which I can later compare (a) whether a learned encoder (scvi, scgpt) helps, (b) whether multiprofile + aggregation adds value, (c) whether image modality adds value, and (d) whether multimodal fusion outperforms either single modality. Choosing the simplest baseline first maximizes the interpretability of every subsequent comparison within the 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: We have only one data point (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), which is a modest baseline. The most critical uncertainty is whether adding the image modality provides any benefit over RNA alone, since this determines whether the entire multimodal search direction is worthwhile. Question: config_016 (multimodal, pca_n2000, resnet50, singleprofile, concat) is the minimal extension of config_001—only the image encoder and fusion are added—so it cleanly isolates the contribution of image information to the existing RNA baseline. Why this is the best next step: With 8 experiments remaining, we must first determine if multimodal is a promising direction before investing budget in exploring aggregation, fusion, encoder, or profile variations within it. A direct head-to-head comparison (same RNA encoder, same profile setting, only image added) gives the highest information gain per experiment and prevents wasting budget on complex multimodal variants if the image signal is weak or unhelpful.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) achieved 0.527 acc, a meaningful +4.2pt gain over RNA-only (config_001, 0.485), confirming that the image modality contributes positively. However, we have no information on whether multiprofile aggregation (avgpool/transformer) can further improve performance beyond singleprofile. Question: config_018 extends config_016 by switching to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation while keeping the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (resnet50), and fusion (concat), isolating the effect of multi-profile aggregation. Why this is the best next experiment: With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether multiprofile helps is the highest-leverage design question because it determines whether the remaining budget should explore the multiprofile branch (configs 018-027, 030-051) or focus on singleprofile variants (fusion, encoder swaps). If multiprofile+avgpool improves on 0.527, we can then test transformer aggregation and weighted fusion as logical extensions. If it does not, we avoid wasting experiments on that branch and pivot to fusion/encoder comparisons within singleprofile.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the current best at 0.619 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation is a major driver (+0.092 over singleprofile). Uncertainty: whether avgpool is the optimal aggregation or whether a transformer-based aggregation could capture richer inter-profile structure. This experiment (config_020) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other settings (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) identical to config_018, cleanly isolating the aggregation effect. This is the best next step because aggregation is the critical bottleneck in multiprofile settings—transformer can model non-linear, position-dependent interactions between profiles that simple averaging cannot—and a single-variable comparison directly tells us whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based configurations or stick with avgpool.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc. We have strong evidence that multimodal + multiprofile + avgpool is the right architecture, but we have only tested concat fusion. Config_019 changes exactly one variable (fusion: concat → weighted) while holding all other settings at their best-known values. This cleanly isolates whether a learned weighted combination of modalities can outperform simple concatenation. It is the most direct exploitation of the current best result with minimal confounding, and with 5 experiments remaining, establishing whether fusion strategy matters before exploring larger changes (image encoder, RNA encoder) ensures we build on the strongest base configuration for subsequent experiments.

Evidence: The current best (config_019, acc=0.639) uses multimodal + multiprofile + pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted. Key findings so far: multimodal > rna-only (+0.04), multiprofile >> singleprofile (+0.09), avgpool > transformer (+0.04), weighted > concat (+0.02). The two major untested axes are the image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) and the RNA encoder (pca vs scvi/scgpt). Question: Does a stronger, larger image encoder (ViT-L) improve on ResNet50 while keeping all other settings at their validated optima? Why this experiment: config_025 is a clean single-variable swap (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) from the current best, isolating the image-encoder effect. ViT-L is a substantially larger pretrained model and the image modality already proved valuable, making this the highest-impact untested dimension. With 4 experiments left, confirming or ruling out the image-encoder axis first will guide whether to invest remaining budget in RNA-encoder variants or further fusion/aggregation tweaks.

The current best (config_019: pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.639 acc, and config_025 (imagenet_vit_l variant) is nearly identical at 0.635, indicating the image encoder is not the bottleneck. The aggregation (avgpool) and fusion (weighted) choices are well-supported. The most impactful unexplored dimension is the RNA encoder—only pca_n2000 has been tested in the multimodal setting. Config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) isolates the effect of replacing PCA with a learned scVI latent representation while holding all other settings at their proven-best values. This is the cleanest single-variable comparison to config_019 and addresses the largest remaining source of uncertainty. With 3 experiments left, identifying whether a better RNA encoder can push past 0.64 is the highest-value question before final exploitation.

The current best (config_031, acc=0.6776) uses scvi_n200 with resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted. The largest single improvement in the search came from switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (+3.86%), while image encoder choice (resnet50 vs ViT) had negligible effect (0.6390 vs 0.6352). The most impactful untested variable is the scgpt RNA encoder, which has never been evaluated in the multimodal setting. Config_043 changes only the RNA encoder (scvi→scgpt) from the current best, isolating its effect. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi, it opens a new direction for the final two experiments; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi as optimal and the remaining budget can focus on minor refinements (e.g., ViT pairing). This is the highest-information experiment given only 2 trials remain.

The best result so far is config_031 (SCVI, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.6776 acc. The evidence strongly supports SCVI as the RNA encoder, avgpool as aggregation, weighted fusion, and multiprofile. The only untested dimension on this best backbone is the image encoder: ResNet50 vs. ViT-L. With PCA, the two image encoders were nearly tied (0.6390 vs 0.6352), but SCVI produces a richer, learned latent representation that may interact differently with a vision transformer's patch-level features. config_037 changes only the image encoder (ResNet50→ViT-L) from the best configuration, cleanly isolating that effect. This is the highest-value single-variable experiment: if ViT-L helps, we find a new best; if not, config_031 remains our top result for the final experiment, where we can either confirm or explore one last tweak.

The current best is config_037 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) at 0.706245. All other design dimensions (model setting, profile, RNA encoder, image encoder, fusion) have been well-explored and their optimal choices identified. The only remaining untested dimension with this top configuration is aggregation: transformer vs. avgpool. While prior evidence (config_018 vs config_020, both with pca_n2000) favors avgpool over transformer by ~4 points, that comparison was made with a weaker RNA encoder. The interaction between transformer aggregation and the stronger scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l representations is untested. As the final experiment, config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) is the highest-value test: it isolates the aggregation effect in the best setting, and if transformer happens to complement the richer representations, it could push accuracy above 0.706. No other untested configuration offers a more direct path to potentially improving on the current best.
